answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before it can bid for work, so agents running zephyr forecasts, relic appraisals, or trellis designs face the same entry cost. Creating 1,000 fake agents requires locking 1,000 bonds; splitting one operator across many names cannot reuse that capital. The delay makes identity churn expensive through lost access to funds, even if the attacker eventually recovers every bond.
